core_obligations: Reduce to an equidimensional X by decomposing into connected components, and write alpha = c cap [X]_n with c in A^*(X) using the identification for a smooth scheme (proof lines 14571-14573).

Compute i_*(i^!(alpha)) by the five-step chain i_*(i^!(c cap [X]_n)) = i_*(c cap i^![X]_n) = i_*(c cap [Y]_e) = c cap i_*[Y]_e = alpha . [Y]_e, invoking the commutation of the Gysin map with bivariant capping, the Gysin pullback of the fundamental class, and the commutation of bivariant classes with proper pushforward (proof lines 14574-14582).
Identify the last expression with the intersection product using the same description of the operational theory (proof lines 14582-14583).
proof_roadmap: Reduce to the equidimensional case and express the class operationally (proof lines 14571-14573).
Run the five-step chain of equalities with each step justified by its own input (proof lines 14574-14582).
Translate back to the intersection product (proof lines 14582-14583).
difficulty_reason: For a field k, a scheme X smooth over k, a regular closed immersion i : Y -> X and a cycle class alpha, the lemma asserts that if Y is equidimensional of dimension e then alpha . [Y]_e = i_*(i^!(alpha)) in CH_*(X) (statement lines 14562-14568). The proof decomposes X into connected components to assume it equidimensional of dimension d, and represents alpha as c cap [X]_n for some c in A^*(X) using the identification of Chow groups with the operational theory for a smooth scheme (proof lines 14571-14573). The identity is then a five-term chain of equalities whose each step is a named input: the choice of c; the commutation of the Gysin map with capping by a bivariant class; the fundamental-class computation i^![X]_d = [Y]_e for a regular closed immersion; the commutation of bivariant classes with proper pushforward; and again the identification of the operational theory with Chow groups (proof lines 14574-14583). Converting an intersection product into the composition of a bivariant capping with the Gysin map, and keeping track of which axiom moves c past i^! and past i_*, is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.
